JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this Petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.2,00,00,000/- for the Death of one Sri.Channabasavanna J. Gujjar in a road traffic accident dated 05.11.2019.
2.
The case of the Petitioners' in brief is that:

On 05.11.2019 the deceased along with Two others by name Rishabh and Gaurav Kataria were traveling in the Car bearing Reg.No.DL4CAV9850 Grand I10 Sportz 1.2,
while so proceeding very late in the night near Khuda Lahora Bridge, Chandigarh, the car hit against a metal electric pole and met SCCH-25 with fatal accident.
The accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the said Car.

After the accident the driver of the Car died on intervening night of 6 th & 7th i.e., on 6.11.2019 about 1.30am and the deceased suffered grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries while on the way to the hospital.
3. It is the further case of the petitioners that, Postmortem was conducted and police handover the dead body to the claimants.
The claimants brought the dead body to Bangalore and cremated.

At the time of accident the deceased was hale and healthy, working as Activities Assistant in private company called Metro Eco Green Resort Ltd., the Oberoi Sikh Vilas, the Oberoi Palanpru Post,
Sialba Majri, New Chandigarh, Punjab - 140 110 and drawing gross salary of Rs.36,129/- per month and he was also getting incentive of Rs.10,000/- per month.
The deceased was the only earning member of the family and only child to the petitioners/claimants.
The petitioners were depending upon the earning of the deceased.
Due to the sudden demise of the SCCH-25 deceased, the petitioners are put to unbearable agony and loss.
The Sarangpur Police, Chandigarh District, have registered a case against the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.DL4CAV 9850 in DDR No.21/2019 and released the dead body to the petitioners.
The accident was solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the said Car.
The respondents being the insured and insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to the service of notice, the Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear hence, placed exparte.

5. The objections of the Respondent No.2:
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of Respondent No.1 to the Private Car bearing Reg.No.DL-4- CAV-9850, it was in force as on the date of accident.

The police did not comply the terms and conditions u/Section SCCH-25 158(6) of M.V.
J.B. Gujjar vs Vimal Monga on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77123509/
2 Act.

sentences.text: The driver of the Car was not holding a valid and effective DL at the time of accident.
It has denied the involvement of the Car in the accident and occurrence of the accident.
Further stated that the deceased had not fastened the seat belt and also was intoxicated by alcohol due to which suffered grievous injuries and succumbed.
Deceased died due to his own negligent act.

Further, denied the age, income,
avocation etc., and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues today:
1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased Sri. Channabasavanna J.
Gujjar?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, the deceased Sri.Channabasavanna J. Gujjar had died due to the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 06.11.2019 on the intervening night at about 01.30am near Kuda Lahora Bridge, Chandigarh, due to SCCH-25 rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.DL-4-CAV-9850 as alleged?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom payable 4.

What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove their case, the Petitioners have examined Petitioner No.1 - Mr. J.B.Gujjar - Father of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.10(a).

On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 got examined its official Mr. Shreyas Bhat as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to 8.
8.
Heard both the Counsels and perused the materials on record.

9. My finding to the above issues are as follows:-
Issue Nos.1 & 2: In the affirmative Issue No.3 : In the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order for the Following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:
SCCH-25

It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the Father,
Petitioner No.2 is the Mother of the deceased - Channabasavanna J. Gujjar.
The Petitioners to prove their relationship have examined the 1st Petitioner as PW.1.
PW.1 has specifically spoken about this relationship in his chief- examination.

Apart from that, to prove the relationship, the Petitioners have produced Inquest Report and PM J.B. Gujjar vs Vimal Monga on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77123509/
3 report as per Exs.P.4 & 5.

entities.text: PM J.B. Gujjar vs Vimal Monga
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Exs.P.4 & 5 - father and mother of the deceased is mentioned as Jayadeo B. Gujjar and Prathibha J. Gujjar who are the petitioner Nos.1 & 2 in the present case.
These documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents.
The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and the documents, this court is of the opinion that the SCCH-25 Petitioner No.1 is the Father, Petitioner No.2 is the Mother of the deceased Channabasavanna J. Gujjar.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:

The Petitioners to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Car have examined Petitioner No.1 as PW.1 and produced documents as per Exs.P.1 to 7.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During his cross examination he has admitted that the accident spot was a curve.
He has admitted that as per FSL report the deceased had alcohol of 44.67%mg in his blood.
He has admitted that as per Exs.P.1 & 2 final reports, spot mahazar and spot sketch are not available.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the involvement and negligence of the insured vehicle.

It has examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R.8 i.e., Authorization letter, insurance policy, OD claim by R-1, Survey report, repudiation letter sent to R-1 with postal SCCH-25 receipt, PM report of the driver, FSL report of driver and FSL report of deceased.
During the cross examination of RW.1 he has stated that Exs.R.6 to 8 were given by the insured.

12. The documents produced by the Petitioners such as the Right to Information Act 2005, dated 17.05.2021 at Ex.P.1, Another letter under RTI issued by DSP cum CPIO HQ at Ex.P.2, Application seeking information dated 25.06.2021 addressed to Dy.SP of Chandigarh with postal receipt and acknowledgment at Ex.P.3, Attested copy of Inquest report at Ex.P.4, Attested copy of PM report at Ex.P.5, Attested copy of Medical legal report dated 07.11.2019 at Ex.P.6 and Attested copy of Examination report at Ex.P.7 are all public documents and have initial presumptive value under law.
These documents fully and completely corroborate with the evidence of PW.1.

In the DDR report at Ex.P.4 and Death Report at Ex.P.9 and General Dairy Details at Ex.P.10, it is mentioned by the police that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the Driver of the Car who was under the influence of alcohol.
Moreover, the Respondent No.2 has not SCCH-25 obtained any contrary admission from the mouth of PW.1 to show the negligence of the deceased.

Therefore, there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence of PW.1.
13.

The Inquest report produced as per Ex.P.4 and PM report produced as per Ex.P.5 clearly shows the cause of death 'Cerebral damage consequent to blunt trauma to head which is sufficient to cause death in an ordinary course of nature'.

J.B. Gujjar vs Vimal Monga on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77123509/
4 14.

entities.text: J.B. Gujjar vs Vimal Monga on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 has contended that the deceased and the driver of the Car were under the influence of alcohol.
In support of the same, they have produced the Exs.R.6 to 8 FSL reports relating to the deceased and the Driver and the PM report of the Driver.
The deceased of this case was sitting in the passenger's seat and the Car was being driven by Gaurav Kartia.
The Respondent No.2 has not shown how the person sitting in the passenger's seat could have caused the accident.
This is a third party claim.

Such being the case, the insurance company cannot escape from SCCH-25 its liability by saying that the insured has breached the terms of the policy by handing over the insured vehicle to a person under the influence of alcohol.
Therefore, this defence of the respondent No.2 is rejected.

On overall perusal of Exs.P.1 to P.7, it is clearly mentioned that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.DL-4-CAV-9850 and hit against a metal electric pole.
Due to impact the deceased suffered injuries and was being taken to the hospital.
In spite of better treatment, the deceased succumbed to the injuries.

Therefore, on the evidence of PW.1 which has remained unimpeached during the cross examination and on the basis of documents on record this Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the offending Car Driver.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No. 3:
PW.1 has specifically spoken before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, they have lost the bread earner of their family and his loving son.
He has SCCH-25 further deposed that he has spent huge amount towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation as per the following discussion.
Monthly income 16.
According to the Petitioners, the deceased was working as Activities Assistant in a Private Company called 'Metro Eco Green Resort Ltd. and earning Rs.36,129/- per month.
He was also getting incentive of Rs.10,000/- per month.
In this regard, the Petitioners have produced Bank Account statement and October 2019 salary slip as per Ex.P.8.
As per Ex.P.8 the salary for the month of November 2019 was Rs.28,071/- and the salary for the month of October 2019 was Rs.32,584/- was credited.
In the Salary slip also the Net Salary is shown as Rs.32,584/-.
Under such circumstances, this court deems it fit to fix the income of the deceased at Rs.32,584/- per month for calculating the compensation.
SCCH-25
Age of the deceased 17.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced PM report as per Ex.P.5.
As per Ex.P.5 the deceased was aged about 28 years.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
This shows that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 28 years.

(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE PROSPECTS:-
J.B. Gujjar vs Vimal Monga on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77123509/
5
As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 17.

entities.text: Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the deceased has a Father and Mother, aged about 66 & 57 years respectively and they are considered as the dependents of the deceased.

As such, the petitioners are entitled to get compensation.
18.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged above 60 years are 14MVC No.4115/2021 SCCH-25 not entitled to any future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As mentioned above, since the deceased was under 40 years age slab, 40% future prospects is to be added to his monthly income.
So Rs.13,033/- (Rs.32,584/- X 40% = Rs.13,033/-) should be added to his monthly salary of Rs.32,584/- then it comes to Rs.45,617/- per month.
As per the Sarala Verma case, if the deceased is a bachelor then 1/2 of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
Therefore, Rs.22,080/- has to deducted then balance comes to Rs.22,809/- (Rs.45,617/- - Rs.22,808/-).
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.46,53,036/- (Rs.22,809/- X 17 x 12) = Rs.46,53,036/-).

(ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:-
In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130

entities.text: Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.

The right to SCCH-25 consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort,
guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".

19. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
20.

entities.text: United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 is the Father and the petitioner No.2 is the Mother of the deceased.
The Mother, father have to live remaining part of their life in the absence of their young son.
The loss of a young son full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to the parents.

However,
petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each (Total Rs.80,000/-) under the head of loss of consortium.
SCCH-25 (iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES AND LOSS OF ESTATE:-
In so far as the funeral and transportation expenses are concerned, the Petitioners have contended that they have spent huge amount towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
But, there is no document produced in this regard.

Therefore, in the interest of justice the Petitioners are awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head.

If the deceased was alive he would have certainly saved some amount out of his living and personal expenses and created an estate in favour of the J.B. Gujjar vs Vimal Monga on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77123509/
6 Petitioners.

entities.text: J.B. Gujjar vs Vimal Monga on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for a total sum of Rs.47,73,036/-.

If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.47,73,100/-
Liability 21.
The respondent No.2 has failed to prove the defences.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer has to SCCH-25 indemnify the respondent No.1.
The petitioners have claimed compensation for a sum of Rs.2,00,00,000/-.
But the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.47,73,100/- along with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.4:-

In view of the findings of the above issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with costs.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensa- tion of Rs.47,73,100/- (Rupees Forty Seven Lakhs Seventy Three Thousand and One Hun- dred only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount and interest.
SCCH-25
The Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the peti- tioners.
The respondent No.2 is liable to deposit compensation to the petitioners within 60 days from the date of suit till its realization.

On deposit of the award amount and inter- est, Rs.10,00,000/- each shall be deposited in the names of the Petitioner Nos.1 & 2 in any Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining amount shall be released to the petitioner Nos.1 & 2 equally by way of e-pay- ment with proper identification and due ac- knowledgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
